items.title: Two guilty, two cleared over failed plot to import 850kg of cocaine
paras: The cocaine was found hidden on a bulk carrier in 2023. ( Supplied: WA Police/AFP/ABF )
Two people have been found guilty over an attempt to smuggle almost a tonne of cocaine into Western Australia.
Ashley Vlotman and Meagan Rees were found guilty of aiding the importation of 850kg of cocaine.
Two other people have been acquitted, while the jury was unable to reach a verdict on another man.
Two people have been found guilty for their roles in a failed attempt to bring nearly a tonne of cocaine into Western Australia, in what the prosecutor described as "disorganised crime".
The drugs, worth half a billion dollars, were found inside the bulk carrier St Pinot, which headed to Australia from Argentina with a load of animal feed in May 2023.
Ashley Vlotman, 40, and Meagan Rees, 35, were today found guilty of aiding the attempted importation of 850 kilograms of cocaine.

The court heard Vlotman and Rees were among the organisers of a plan to get a boat to rendezvous with the bulk carrier, but the operation came apart when the crew of the smaller vessel hit trouble in rough seas and had to be rescued.

Three men were on board that smaller boat, named No Fixed Address, and earlier this year one of them — Tamaohungia Joseph Tepatu-Edwards — was sentenced to 26 years in prison after pleading guilty over the attempted importation.
Authorities staged a press conference after the drugs were seized. ( ABC News: Dave Weber )
One of the other men on board, Lithuanian Germanas Joneliunas, was acquitted over his involvement, saying he believed it was a tobacco importation.
The jury could not reach a unanimous verdict on the other man on No Fixed Address, Terrence Baker, who said he believed he was going on a fishing trip to Rottnest.
The captain of St Pinot, 46-year-old Milan Begovic, told the court he did not know there was cocaine on his vessel and the jury found him not guilty.
The WA Supreme Court heard the criminal scheme was beset by multiple failures and the cocaine did not actually make it to shore until after the authorities had taken control.
The roles of Vlotman and Rees were outlined in messages shown to the jury.
Meagan Rees pictured outside court during the trial. ( ABC News: David Weber )
While there was no mention of cocaine, there were messages about buying a boat, with someone using the handle Meagan Elizabeth saying "I'm charging an administrator fee" for being a "messenger".
Tepatu-Edwards and Mr Baker set out on No Fixed Address with Mr Joneliunas, a man from Lithuania they had never met before.
Mr Baker and Mr Joneliunas told the court they became violently ill at sea, and some hours later, No Fixed Address itself was in trouble.
Mr Baker called his mother and Water Police became involved with Tactical Response Group officers boarding the boat.
No drugs were found on No Fixed Address and the trio were released before being arrested again after the cocaine was found on St Pinot.
St Pinot had been boarded and directed to port by the authorities, with the cocaine discovered in packages inside a flooded ballast tank.
In messages to a friend after the arrests, Meagan Elizabeth referred to a "syndicate", and said the police already seemed to know a lot.
Prosecutor Steven Whybrow labelled the plot an "embarrassment to organised crime".
After the jury delivered its verdicts, Justice Amanda Forrester said Mr Begovic and Mr Joneliunas were free to leave, although it's understood they do not have visas to stay in Australia.

items.title: Jobs cuts will diminish Tasmanian museum, historian says
paras: Earlier this month, the Launceston City Council said it was changing its "organisational structure". ( ABC News: Morgan Timms )
Four history staff with a combined 90 years of experience have been made redundant from Launceston's Queen Victoria Museum and Art Gallery (QVMAG).
The cuts come as the Launceston City Council scraps 10 full-time equivalent management roles in order to find savings.
The Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery (TMAG) in Hobart is also facing job losses, and a motion to reverse job cuts is due to be raised in parliament this week.
Four Queen Victoria Museum and Art Gallery (QVMAG) staff with a combined experience of 90 years have been made redundant, as part of a restructure by the City of Launceston.
The Launceston City Council will cut 10 full-time equivalent jobs as it aims to save about $1.9 million a year.

The ABC understands this includes roles in QVMAG's history department, including a senior curator, assistant curator and a technical officer, along with another technical officer from the museum's archives.
Staff at Launceston's Queen Victoria Museum and Art Gallery will be impacted by the redundancies. ( ABC News: Morgan Timms )
Oral History Tasmania President Jill Cassidy told 936 ABC Hobart that as a result of the cuts, there would be no-one left in the history department, aside from one archivist.

"I know just how much the collections of the museum have been bolstered by all those people around Tasmania, but particularly the Launceston area, who expect that their collections will be looked after," Ms Cassidy said.
Jill Cassidy says there is an expectation the public collections would be looked after. ( ABC News: Damian McIntyre )
"The council just really needs to look at itself to find out how this could be happening; that so much experience should be booted out the door with no thought of what the future will hold."
Launceston historian John Dent said while the museum's online portal was useful, local historians would still need to access information through staff.
"So it's necessary to talk to the people and the staff at QVMAG to be able to get access to a lot of this information that they have such an extensive collective 90 years experience in.
"It's going to diminish the accessibility of the collection and it's going to be much harder and more difficult for [remaining] staff to respond.
"You cut culture, you don't see the value that it adds to our community. But these cultural institutions, it's what we are."
John Dent says the staff cuts to the QVMAG will "diminish the accessibility of the collection". ( ABC News: Damian McIntyre )
Earlier in November, the council said in a statement it was changing its "organisational structure" and was working with the affected employees.
The Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery has nearly a million items from the state collection in its care. ( ABC News: Ebony ten Broeke )
Jobs at Tasmania's state-owned museum the Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery (TMAG) are also in question.
In August, staff at TMAG said they were informed nearly 20 jobs were due to be cut.
The state government said the claims were false, but conceded there would be job cuts across the department overseeing TMAG, including at the gallery.
Independent Member for Nelson Meg Webb is raising a motion in parliament's Upper House this week calling on the government to reverse the decision.

"I am hopeful my upper house colleagues will see fit this week to add their voices to those local, national and international calls for an urgent rethink and reversal of these funding cuts," Ms Webb said.

items.title: Woolworths orders $100k returned to workers over supply chain underpayments
paras: Workplace abuses at a small number of blueberry farms have caused reputational damage to the sector. ( ABC News )
Supermarkets and the NSW government have reacted to a new report from the state's Anti-Slavery Commissioner, which alleged illegal activity from labour hire syndicates.
The NSW government has announced a new modern slavery taskforce to share information between agencies.
Political and industry figures are calling for state licensing of labour hire firms.

As the NSW government forms a taskforce to investigate modern slavery, the ABC has learnt compliance checks by supermarket giant Woolworths uncovered more than $100,000 in underpayments to workers by its fruit and vegetable suppliers in the past financial year.

The taskforce was announced just days after the NSW Anti-Slavery Commissioner's response to a parliamentary inquiry into modern slavery was tabled, alleging some labour hire syndicates were involved in criminal activities.

James Cockayne's report detailed how they skirted around enforcement and avoided inspections, confirming to the ABC those allegations had been referred to the Australian Federal Police and NSW Police.
Blueberry farms are reliant on migrant labour during picking season. ( ABC News )

The report, which criticised police for taking a reactive approach to labour hire syndicates, recommended that organisations review their supply chains for any connection to the businesses identified.
Woolworths told the ABC it had this year extended its human rights checks beyond its direct suppliers to the growers who supply them.
A spokesperson said in a statement that, when problems were found, Woolworths could oversee repayments to workers by suppliers, set suppliers deadlines to fix issues, or end a supply relationship.
"As a result of our compliance initiatives in [the 2025-26 financial year], more than $100,000 was returned to workers in our fruit and vegetable supply chain," they said.
"We also run a 'Speak Up' line and encourage workers to contact Woolworths directly about any concerns over their workplace and conditions.
A Coles spokesperson told the ABC it was taking modern slavery seriously. ( ABC Coffs Coast: Claire Simmonds )
Coles also issued a statement to the ABC saying it did "not tolerate any forms of worker exploitation".
"Compliance with Coles' Ethical Sourcing Policy and applicable workplace laws is a condition of trade for suppliers," a spokesperson said.
The NSW government today announced a Modern Slavery Taskforce to bring together state agencies, regulatory bodies and law enforcement agencies.
Members will be drawn from state agencies of NSW Police, SafeWork, industrial relations, the Department of Communities and Justice, local councils and the Migrant Workers Centre.
Federal representatives from the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations and Fair Work Ombudsman will also be invited to join.
The NSW government announced it will set up a taskforce to share information between agencies on modern slavery concerns. ( AAP: Bianca De Marchi )
NSW Industrial Relations Minister Sophie Cotsis said the taskforce would ensure "better coordination between agencies and law enforcement bodies to stamp out the exploitation of migrant workers".
The government has also promised, if re-elected next year, to introduce a labour hire licensing scheme and require all businesses to use only licensed providers.
Queensland, Victoria, South Australia and the ACT already have labour hire licensing schemes.
James Cockayne made several allegations about how labour hire syndicates were skirting enforcement operations. ( ABC News )
Dr Cockayne welcomed the taskforce decision, saying there were "a number of labour hire syndicates exploiting migrant workers in rural and regional NSW".
Berries Australia chief executive Rachel Mackenzie said the taskforce could help enforce criminal laws until all political parties committed to state regulation of labour hire.
She said there was no shortage of intelligence about abuse of workers, but enforcement was lacking.
"Having the police involved in this taskforce is a positive step," Ms Mackenzie said.
Rachel McKenzie says Berries Australia welcomes more enforcement in the industry. ( ABC News )
Brooke Lord, advocacy spokesperson for the Recruitment, Consulting and Staffing Association, said the labour hire industry welcomed the taskforce.
"It frustrates us no end that these kinds of activities continue to operate under the radar," she said.
"Anything that will help us identify these people and stamp out this behaviour is a welcome development."
Brooke Lord says she is frustrated the actions of dodgy operators are damaging the reputations of her members. ( Supplied: Recruiting, Consulting and Staffing Association )
Ms Lord said the taskforce needed to hold the wider supply chain accountable.
"We do have people who continue to buy services from people who are less expensive in market, who persist in creating a market for these dodgy operators," she said.
"I really hope that the actions of the taskforce will [target] the dodgy operators, but also those people who are buying services they know probably don't smell quite right."
Officials from Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Tax Office and Australian Border Force during raids in the Riverina in July 2026. ( Supplied: Fair Work Ombudsman )
Modern Slavery Committee chair Joe McGirr said the taskforce was a positive step, as government agencies have operated in silos for too long.
Joe McGirr welcomes a taskforce as a method to bring agencies together. ( ABC News: Lauren Pezet )
"One of the issues that was a concern to the committee has been the sharing of information between different government departments," he said.
"Perpetrators of modern slavery, disreputable labour hire firms and people flying under the radar, have often been able to escape detection.
"The key issue is the labour hire regulation, and I think there is a strong bipartisan support for it," he said.

items.title: Meldrum remembered as 'the fan all artists wish to have'
paras: An "unwavering" champion. "Truly unique." An "enemy" turned ally. And "the fan all artists wish to have".

Australian musicians have been lining up to pay tribute to Ian "Molly" Meldrum, the music tastemaker, record producer, Countdown host and Hey, Hey It's Saturday regular who died at the age of 83 on Monday morning.

Meldrum, who leaves a lasting legacy as one of the most influential figures in the Australian media landscape, was introduced to a whole generation of Australians as the face of the ABC's Countdown TV show.
Among those watching at home was a young Kylie Minogue, who reflected on growing up watching the program "every single weekend" long before she was Australian pop royalty.
"[I was] in awe of the show and the magic it brought to our little TV in the lounge room and dreaming of how music might become part of my life," Minogue wrote in a heartfelt Instagram tribute.
"I was over the Moon to be in the Countdown audience one time, and by my late teens I was on the show."
Meldrum was an early, staunch supporter of Minogue's transition from Neighbours soap star to an international career in music .

She praised his "unwavering love and support" of her, as well as the way Meldrum "championed so many Aussie artists and welcomed international artists to Australia in his own wonderful and inimitable way".

In his own online tribute, fellow Neighbours star turned solo artist Jason Donovan called Meldrum "a truly unique character, a great Australian and one of this country's greatest pioneers and ambassadors for music and entertainment.
"He was loved, recognised and respected around the world for the extraordinary contribution he made to Australian music and the artists he championed. There will never be another quite like him."
He also shared a memory of Meldrum appearing in a Neighbours episode alongside Minogue and Guy Pearce: "What a day that was!"
Jimmy Barnes said he and Meldrum "went through a lot", and initially considered him "the enemy", as the host of "the best music TV show in the country but insisting that we had to mime".
However, after appearing on Countdown, Barnes conceded the impact on Cold Chisel's career was immediate, catapulting them to bigger venues and wider popularity.
Mysterious Girl hit-maker Peter Andre, who signed to Meldrum's label, Melodian Records, in the early 90s as a teenager, said his death "really hurts," calling him a "true icon [and] friend".
"If it wasn't for this man, I would not of had any of the chances I had to make it in any way in the entertainment industry back when it was near impossible to get noticed," he wrote.
ARIA Hall of Famer Kate Ceberano also praised Meldrum for helping elevate and amplify her career, saying his death marked the end of an era.
"He had no agenda he wanted, no praise, he never basked in any reflected glory or self pride," she wrote.
"He simply wanted the world to hear what he could hear, wanted you to see what he was looking at and then blow it up to 11. Way up sky high. No dream is too big. No cringe, withholding nothing."
Before Countdown aired, Meldrum produced Russell Morris's 1969 single The Real Thing, transforming the song penned by the late Johnny Young into a six-minute, chart-topping epic
"He was a unique, and loveable individual," Morris wrote on Faceboook . "I was lucky enough to call him my friend, and mentor."
He added: "As can be witnessed by his incredible musical, and media career — he achieved things that were truly great… long live the king."
Icehouse frontman Iva Davies called Meldrum a "bright, larger than life figure", remembering his support in championing homegrown artists and their careers.
"Like the rest of the music community that owed so much to his support, the band and I are so thankful that Molly was a part of our lives and music," he wrote.
Similarly, Daddy Cool and Mondo Rock musician Ross Wilson wrote that Meldrum "selflessly helped me and so many other performers".
"The band and I are so thankful that Molly was a part of our lives and music."

items.title: No life jackets, lifeboat or functioning radio on airboat during 2023 crash
paras: The star of a popular Netflix series, Matt Wright is known for his work as a celebrity crocodile wrangler. ( Supplied: National Geographic/Outback Wrangler )
Matt Wright's tourism company, Top End Safari Camp, has pleaded guilty to breaching NT work safety laws over a 2023 airboat crash.
Several people were injured, including one passenger who suffered skull fractures and a scalp laceration.
Darwin Local Court has heard the company is close to financial collapse, with the case returning to court in December.
A court has heard passengers on an airboat tour, operated by Matt Wright's outback adventure company, were forced to use their clothes and towels to treat injuries after a serious crash.
Today, Top End Safari Camp pleaded guilty to breaching NT WorkSafe laws over the May 2023 airboat crash.
Wright, a director of the company, attended Darwin Local Court for today's hearing, however, his wife and co-director, Kaia Wright, was unable to attend due to illness.
Matt and Kaia Wright leaving the NT Supreme Court last August, after he was found guilty on two counts of attempting to pervert the course of justice. ( ABC News: Michael Parfitt )
The court heard the boat, which was carrying 13 passengers including six children, crashed into a semi-submerged tree while travelling along Sweets Lagoon in Bynoe, south-west of Darwin.
The force of the collision threw passengers forward out of their seats, causing injuries to several people.
One passenger, who the court heard was seated in the front row of the boat, hit her head on a step, which caused serious head injuries.
"A significant portion of her scalp was opened," prosecutor Nicholas Goodfellow said.
Nicholas Goodfellow says several passengers were injured in the accident. ( ABC News: Randi Dahnial )
The court heard in the immediate aftermath of the crash, crew realised the boat did not have a first-aid kit on board.
At the time, the airboat was not fitted with life jackets, a lifeboat or a functioning radio, the court heard.
Matt Wright is widely known for his work as a celebrity crocodile wrangler, having appeared on multiple television shows. ( ABC News: Randi Dahnial )

The lawyer representing Top End Safari Camp, Lyma Nguyen, said the company's failure to comply with its safety duties was "not systemic", describing the breach as an "anomaly" and a "one-off incident".

Ms Nguyen also told the court Mr and Mrs Wright were interstate on the day of the crash and were relying on their general manager, Tim Johnson, and the airboat master, Anton Pugliuca, to manage the tours.
The maximum fine for the company's breach is $1.5 million, with Ms Nguyen urging the court to consider Top End Safari Camp's "precarious financial situation".
Ms Nguyen said Wright and the company were facing several civil claims in the NT Supreme Court and Federal Court, brought by several of the airboat passengers.
Lyma Nguyen urged the court to take the company's'precarious financial situation into account. ( ABC News: Randi Dahnial )
"The company has been operating at a loss due to reputation damage arising out of the crash and the prosecutions, and the company has a very limited capacity to pay a fine.

items.title: RBI imposes monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited
paras: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 17, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on Fusion Finance Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of directions issued by RBI on ‘Know Your Customer (KYC)’ and ‘Internal Ombudsman’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under section 58G(1)(b) read with section 58B(5)(aa) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its financial position as on March 31, 2026. Based on the supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for failure to comply with the RBI directions. After considering the company's reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty: The company failed to obtain PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form 60 from customers, while establishing an account-based relationship with those customers; and, The company failed to escalate the partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time. This action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of this monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1537

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: The brain benefits of letting children do things on their own
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print Independence is good for the developing brain Natalia Lebedinskaia/Getty Images Recently, I needed to post a letter. The postbox is at the end of my street, across a small T-junction. It occurred to me that I could send my eldest, who is 8, by herself to post it, but anxiety about letting her out of my sight and across a road immediately kicked in.

It reminded me of the widely publicised case of Karyann Parkinson, a mother in Virginia who was convicted in September of a misdemeanour after allowing her 5-year-old son to walk 800 metres to collect feathers near a pond.

The responses to that story in my parent group were mostly of the “I would never” or “He could have drowned” variety. But increasingly, I have been wondering about the other side of this calculation – in keeping my daughter super-safe, am I giving her enough opportunities to build a brain that can cope with adversity? Could my protective instincts be contributing to some of the anxieties I see bubbling away in her?
To find out, I spoke to Peter Gray , a psychologist and neurologist at Boston College, whose new book, Restoring Childhood: How to set kids free in the age of anxiety , piqued my interest.

His ideas are provocative. He believes that our preoccupation with smartphones and social media as the main cause of declining mental health in children risks us overlooking another major contributor: their dwindling opportunities to play independently from adults.

Children are born dependent on their parents, Gray points out, but also with a strong drive for independence. “Getting away from your parents, doing things on your own, getting into trouble, figuring out how to get yourself out of trouble. This is how children develop resilience, confidence, the agency, the sense that ‘Yeah, I can handle myself’.”

But we no longer allow them to do that, he says. “They go into their teenage years frightened, anxious, not able to deal with the bumps in the road of life because they haven’t had the ever- gradually increasing experience doing that growing up.”

It is certainly an intriguing idea. Rates of anxiety and depression in school-aged children are at an all-time high in the US, leading three US children’s health organisations to declare children’s mental health a national emergency in 2021. Meanwhile, over a quarter of parents in the UK say their child has struggled with anxiety or experienced a panic attack over the past year.

And while social media and screen time are likely to contribute, analyses of the results from several studies on the effects of screen time suggest the harms are fairly small and highly nuanced. “It’s important to look elsewhere,” says Gray.

Intuitively his arguments make sense. Allowing children to play, roam and engage in independent behaviours without direct oversight from adults offer opportunities to develop the three psychological pillars that support good mental health: autonomy, competence and friendship.

Gray argues that we satisfy all three needs by letting kids play together without adult supervision . “When children play [unrestricted], they’re at the cutting edge of their abilities, they’re becoming good at the things they like to do and can see progress, and they make friends doing it.”

What interests me is whether reduced opportunities to play independently could also shape the developing brain. Animal studies suggest that might be the case. For instance, in a 2022 experiment, researchers prevented young rats from playing with each other and then returned them to normal social housing. As adults, they had atypical neural circuitry involved in decision-making and flexible behaviour . Other animal studies in rodents and marmosets show that a lack of play also affects circuits involved in mood and stress responses .

This suggests that play may help our brain develop a healthy stress response – and it will certainly give me pause for thought when I must next decide whether to push my children to do homework over going to the park. But what about the independence aspect? Should I let them go to the park by themselves?

To understand why independent play matters, we need to think about our internal “locus of control” (LOC), says Gray. This is the tendency to believe we have control over our life and can solve problems when they arise. A low internal LOC is associated with a greater risk of anxiety and depression in children and adults.

To see why this is relevant, consider this experiment. Rats who had some control over an unpleasant experience – an electric shock – saw changes in the medial prefrontal cortex , a brain region involved in suppressing stress-related neural activity. These changes seemed to offer some protection against the effects of later, uncontrollable stressors, compared with rodents that had no control over the initial electric shocks.

Gray reckons that, just like these rats, being given an opportunity to feel in control of your life and its challenges helps form an internal LOC that changes the brain in ways that protect you further down the line. “Children develop [a LOC] by practising controlling their own lives – and we’re not allowing children to have that practice.”

Of course, experiments on lab animals can’t prove that climbing too high on playground equipment before finding your own way down, or resolving disagreements over Pokémon cards without adult intervention can protect us from anxiety and depression. But they do offer an intriguing biological explanation for why discovering we can cope with risky situations or that we have some modicum of control over negative experiences when we are young might influence how we respond to later-life stress and adversity.

And although it comes only from correlations, we see support for this idea in human research, too. Young children who have a greater amount of unstructured play score more highly on emotional control and self-regulation later in life than children who played like this less frequently, for instance. Likewise, elementary schools that have longer recesses tend to have higher pupil wellbeing – and not to the detriment of academic success, either.
Cause and effect remain difficult to disentangle, of course: anxious parents may limit a child’s freedom while also passing on a genetic predisposition to anxiety, say, among other factors.

And what about the dangers of letting kids play by themselves? Gray challenges the assumption that the world is more dangerous to kids these days than it used to be. “In fact, crimes against children are way down [in the US],” he says. In terms of non-fatal violent crimes outside the home, that is true. These declined by 85 per cent between 1993 and 2022, according to Bureau of Justice Statistics . Similarly encouraging stats exist in the UK. Road safety is another concern, but the crime statistics alone challenge some of the assumptions that childhood has become universally more dangerous.

So, while I’m not entirely ruling out the effects of social media and other influences on declining mental health in children, I’m certainly persuaded that declining independence could be an integral factor – and unlike social media, it’s something I feel fully in control of.

Starting with that solo trip to the postbox. One errand won’t substantially change my daughter’s developing brain, but it does give her something my reassuring words alone cannot: the experience of doing something that feels a little risky and discovering that she’s able to cope. She returned with a story about a car that stopped to let her cross and how she remembered to say thank you. To her, it was a small adventure. I hope it’s the first step of many that will increase her resilience and protect her brain from the bigger adversities ahead.

items.title: November 23, 1997: The day Novotna beat Pierce to triumph at WTA Finals and overcome a major hurdle
paras: On this day in tennis history, Jana Novotna won the women’s year-end championships to pave the way for her Grand Slam breakthrough months later On this day, November 23, 1997, Jana Novotna defeated Mary Pierce in the final of the WTA year-end championships (7-6, 6-2, 6-3) to claim the first major title of her career.

The Czech had been one of the best players in the world over the past five years, but on several big occasions stumbled in the moment of truth. The confidence she accumulated thanks to this success probably helped her to win her first and only Grand Slam singles title six months later at Wimbledon .

Jana Novotna was born in the Czech Republic – then called Czechoslovakia – in 1968. With her serve-and-volley game, she broke into the top 100 in 1987 before claiming her first WTA title in 1988 in Adelaide, Australia by defeating Jana Pospisilova (7-5, 6-4).

items.title: Greg Rusedski confirms if he’s interested in becoming Great Britain’s next Davis Cup captain
paras: Greg Rusedski has been one of the names mentioned as a potential successor for the vacant Great Britain Davis Cup captaincy role.
Last week, Leon Smith confirmed he would be stepping down as Davis Cup captain for Great Britain, having spent 16 years in that role.

Since this announcement, there has been a lot of speculation about who could fill this role, with many suggesting three-time Grand Slam champion Andy Murray as the likely next Davis Cup captain . It has since been reported that Murray is not ready to take this role, and now another former British number one in Rusedski has confirmed if he would be interested in it instead. “I think any British tennis player would love to have that job, you know it’s an honour obviously to captain your country having obviously played for 13 years, which I think is the longest streak year to year to play,” said Rusedski.

items.title: Carlos Alcaraz makes comment about Jannik Sinner straight after winning the ATP Finals
paras: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals for the first time in Turin, a tournament that was notably missing Jannik Sinner. Alcaraz had never won the ATP Finals before this year, having come closest to doing so in 2025 when he lost in the final to Sinner .

Alcaraz knows exactly what it is like to struggle with injury, having missed nearly five months of competition this year. Following Alcaraz beating Zverev in the final of the ATP Finals, he was asked just how he feels about not having his biggest rival around him on tour right now.

After Alcaraz won the Australian Open this year, either he or Sinner had won the last nine consecutive Grand Slam titles. The two players faced each other in many of these finals, but this year one of Alcaraz or Sinner has been missing from Roland Garros , Wimbledon and the US Open .

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
